_about: The two fit checks. The meter has one segment per item and the call to action appears once all but one are ticked.

services.title: This works when
items: You have a functioning business and a specific commercial problem.
Someone with budget authority is in the room.
The system will run in production, in front of customers or under audit.
You want the people who scope the work to be the people who build it.
You would rather be told the scope is smaller than you budgeted than be told the budget is achievable.
not: Teams looking for additional capacity rather than a partner.
Work where the brief is fixed and the constraint is not open to question.
Procurement run as a lowest-bid comparison against a specification that is not open to revision.
Companies without an operation for the system to run inside, where any answer we gave would be a forecast rather than a finding.

diagnostic.title: It is useful when
items: You are considering a build and want the constraint established before it is scoped
A previous pilot worked in demo and did not survive contact with the operation
Two parts of the business report different numbers for the same thing
A vendor has quoted you for a system and you want the quote tested against the problem rather than against its own specification
A system already shipped and the saving it was meant to produce has not appeared in the numbers
Budget is allocated to technology and there is no settled view internally on where it should land
not: The brief is fixed and the constraint is not open to question
The decision has already been made and what is wanted is a document that supports it
The operation the system would run inside does not exist yet, because there is nothing to examine and the answer would be a forecast rather than a finding
